header.encoding: fixed-width unsigned integers in little-endian byte order

trailer.coverage: all 44 header bytes followed by every payload byte, starting at magic offset 0 and excluding all 4 trailer bytes

flags.name: SYNTHETIC
flags.description: Data payload was produced by the deterministic test source.

flags.name: GAP_BEFORE
flags.description: At least one item or frame was dropped before this data frame.

flags.name: EPOCH_START
flags.description: This is the first frame for this stream in a new run.

flags.name: OVERRUN_BEFORE
flags.description: Firmware lost one or more logical items before this frame; GAP_BEFORE is also required.

flags.name: RESPONSE_ERROR
flags.description: The response prefix reports a nonzero error code.

compatibility.rule: V1/v2 bytes and behaviors remain unchanged. V3 is explicitly selected before a session; no automatic production serial negotiation is added. All frames in a v3 session have version 3. Private versions 0x82/0x83 are never public encodings.

checksum_algorithms.name: ADLER32
checksum_algorithms.description: Adler-32, initial value 1, modulus 65521; mandatory for control and data; covers the transmitted header, encoding prefix and encoded sample bytes, excluding trailer.

aux_bank_mode.name: DISABLED
aux_bank_mode.description: Retain the protocol-v1 D6-through-D13 one-byte input bank and all default behavior.

aux_bank_mode.name: INPUT
aux_bank_mode.description: Configure all of D16 through D23 as a second non-driving input bank and publish one little-endian 16-bit GPIO item.

capability_semantics.profiles: CPU and rate records define known IDs and clocks, not permission to select their Cartesian product. Only a byte-exact settings record in configurations is selectable. Devices may advertise a nonempty subset of the canonical selectable_configurations, including defaults; every nonreserved setting participates even when its stream is disabled.
capability_semantics.tables: Fixed capacity: 2 CPU records, 1 rate record, 64 complete settings records. Counts select leading valid records; all bytes of unused records MUST be zero (including normally nonzero fields). Reject zero counts, counts above capacity, duplicate IDs/tuples, unknown IDs, inconsistent clock/rate/width/policy fields or defaults absent from configurations. CPU/rate definitions can be known without appearing in a selectable tuple. No trailing extension bytes in v3.
capability_semantics.identity: Only Teensy 4.0/IMXRT1062 is defined. simulated=1 identifies emulated board metadata; hardware_serial must start SIM- in that case. nul_ascii fields require printable ASCII, one terminator and all-zero trailing padding; hardware_serial, firmware_version and build_id are nonempty. INFO clocks report active settings; GET_SETTINGS also returns these clocks.
capability_semantics.limits: Advertised limits equal the canonical v3 bounds; smaller hardware queues are internal. All bounds apply before allocation/decompression. Capability response itself is bounded by max_control_frame_bytes.

framing_rules.validation: Require magic 0xDEADBEEF, version 3, header_length 44, reserved zero, known kind/flags/checksum, total_length=44+payload_length+4 and exact fixed schema length for controls. No padding except explicit reserved fields. Every reserved scalar/bit and unused table byte is zero; receivers reject violations.
framing_rules.correlation: Requests use nonzero u32 request_id, zero run_id/sequence/first_sample_ticks/item_count and flags=0. Responses echo request_id and the paired kind; generic ERROR_RESPONSE echoes an unknown rejected kind. Response run_id is current/most recent run (0 before first START); other data-only fields are zero. START response carries the newly assigned run_id. Host must not reuse request IDs during a connection; no automatic retransmission. Device rejects duplicate IDs still in its bounded last-16 accepted-request window with INVALID_REQUEST_ID; older IDs have no replay guarantee. The replay window contains request IDs after dispatch (including command errors), excluding zero and duplicate IDs; it is cleared on a new transport connection. A response with request_id=0 is only valid for INVALID_REQUEST_ID on a zero-ID request.
framing_rules.errors: OK prefix means response_status=0,error_code=0,RESPONSE_ERROR clear and full success payload. Error means response_status=1, nonzero defined error_code, RESPONSE_ERROR set and exactly response_prefix (4 bytes); generic ERROR_RESPONSE alone adds rejected_kind (8 bytes total). Errors never mutate settings, run ID or acquisition state.
framing_rules.malformed: Discard untrusted framing/oversize lengths/checksum failures and resynchronize to magic without allocating from untrusted length. A checksummed bounded request gets a correlated error for invalid payload/flags/request ID or unknown kind. Unsupported protocol versions are outside the v3 session and are discarded, never interpreted as an encoding.
validation_order: reserved fields, data-only request header fields and enum/scalar validity

command_semantics.INFO: Allowed in all states; identity and active clock snapshot; no mutation.
command_semantics.GET_CAPABILITIES: Allowed in all states; fixed capacity definitions, exact selectable settings and board defaults; no mutation.
command_semantics.GET_SETTINGS: Allowed in all states; active complete settings and clocks, retained across STOP; no mutation.
command_semantics.CONFIGURE: STOPPED only, pending_frames=0 and no transport data tail. Validate the entire candidate before any clock/pin/settings changes; on application failure roll back all changes and return INTERNAL_ERROR. Success atomically replaces settings and returns exact requested settings plus corresponding clocks. RUNNING returns INVALID_STATE; DRAINING returns BUSY. Unsupported tuple returns UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION; valid but contradictory rate/width/policy fields return UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION; unknown enums/nonzero reserved bytes return INVALID_PAYLOAD. No partial mutation.
command_semantics.START: STOPPED only with drain complete; reboot defaults are already configured, so explicit CONFIGURE is optional. RUNNING returns INVALID_STATE, DRAINING returns BUSY. Increment u32 run_id modulo 2^32 skipping zero; reset per-stream sequence, relative timestamps and counters. Return exact active settings and clocks before any new-run data. Settings/wire mode are immutable throughout the run.
command_semantics.STOP: RUNNING stops production and enters DRAINING if complete queued frames or a partial transport tail remain, otherwise STOPPED. Repeated STOP in DRAINING/STOPPED is idempotent. Response reports state/pending complete-or-partial frames and current run_id. Preserve settings and final counters. Continue sending queued complete old-run frames without truncation; automatically enter STOPPED only after every data byte is transmitted. Host drains through ordered GET_STATUS response reporting STOPPED,pending_frames=0 before restarting/reconfiguring.
command_semantics.GET_STATUS: STATUS uses existing GET_STATUS ID. Allowed in all states; snapshot of state, run_id, pending frames and per-stream run counters. Produced includes dropped; items are logical ADC pairs/GPIO samples regardless of encoding. Counters are u64 saturating, reset only on successful START or reboot; dropped <= produced. Queued/draining frames count as produced. STOPPED requires pending_frames=0; DRAINING requires pending_frames>0.
command_semantics.reboot: Reset to STOPPED, run_id=0, empty queues/counters/replay history and board defaults. Settings are session-only, never persisted. CDC reconnect preserves settings/state; a host must query and STOP/drain as necessary. Wire version changes require a separate stopped, drained session; CONFIGURE wire_version is always 3.
command_semantics.unsupported_commands: IDs reserved from v1/v2 are not implemented in v3; return generic ERROR_RESPONSE with UNKNOWN_FRAME_KIND. No auxiliary OUTPUT, 528 MHz profile, higher sampling rates or additional boards are selectable.

data_semantics.prefix: Every data payload begins with the 12-byte data_prefix, followed by encoded samples. item_count counts logical ADC pairs or GPIO samples, never runs or encoded bytes. decoded_bytes=item_count*item_bytes; require 1<=item_count<=kind/width maximum before multiplication or allocation. ADC item_bytes=4; GPIO item_bytes=active gpio_width_bits/8. run_count=0 for RAW/PACK12.
data_semantics.raw: encoding=RAW: exactly decoded_bytes sample bytes. ADC pairs are ADC0 u16 LE followed by ADC1 u16 LE; reject either value above 4095. GPIO is one byte or u16 LE; primary D6..D13 bits 0..7, auxiliary D16..D23 bits 8..15. GPIO width must match settings.
data_semantics.rle: encoding=GPIO_RLE only for GPIO with RLE_AUTO policy. Each record is nonzero u16 LE run length followed by one 8-bit or one u16 LE value. 1<=run_count<=item_count; sample byte length exactly run_count*(2+item_bytes). Sum lengths with checked arithmetic, reject prefix sum exceeding item_count and final sum not equal to item_count. Adjacent records must have different values (maximal runs; max logical count is below 65536). No terminator or padding. Require encoded sample bytes < decoded_bytes; tie/expansion falls back to RAW. RAW policy never emits RLE; RLE_AUTO accepts RAW fallback.
data_semantics.pack12: encoding=ADC_PACK12 only for ADC with PACK12 policy. ADC0=a, ADC1=b, each 0..4095; exactly 3*item_count bytes. b0=a&255; b1=(a>>8)|((b&15)<<4); b2=b>>4. Decode a=b0|((b1&15)<<8), b=(b1>>4)|(b2<<4). Reject out-of-range input before packing; never mask invalid codes. PACK12 policy always emits PACK12; RAW ADC policy always emits RAW.
data_semantics.bounds: Wire payload length includes prefix; checksum covers transmitted bytes, never expanded bytes. Max decoded and encoded sample bytes 4048; max wire frame 4108. Lengths and encoding-kind-policy combinations are validated before expansion. No zero-item data frames, truncated records, excess bytes or unknown encodings.
data_semantics.time_and_loss: Data request_id=0; run_id nonzero and equal to START. Each stream has independent u32 sequence starting 0 and incremented for every produced frame including dropped frames, modulo 2^32. EPOCH_START marks its first transmitted frame; GAP_BEFORE marks any logical gap, OVERRUN_BEFORE implies GAP_BEFORE. SYNTHETIC iff source=SYNTHETIC. first_sample_ticks is u64 START-relative in the 8 MHz domain, aligned to 8 ticks, unaffected by encoding. ADC0[i]=first+8*i, ADC1[i]=first+8*i+4; GPIO[i]=first+8*i. Contiguous frames advance by prior item_count*8; any omitted logical samples advance timestamps and set loss flags. No timestamp wrap within a run; stop before u64 overflow. Frames need not cover equal durations across streams.

error_semantics.UNSUPPORTED_VERSION: Reserved legacy meaning; mismatched version is discarded before v3 command dispatch.
error_semantics.UNKNOWN_FRAME_KIND: Checksummed request with unsupported kind, including reserved legacy commands; generic ERROR_RESPONSE carries rejected_kind.
error_semantics.INVALID_LENGTH: Bounded checksummed request has wrong schema payload length. Unbounded/untrusted framing is discarded.
error_semantics.INVALID_PAYLOAD: Nonzero reserved fields, unknown enum values, zero stream mask, out-of-domain scalar or nonzero data-only request header fields.
error_semantics.UNSUPPORTED_CHECKSUM: Reserved legacy meaning; only Adler-32 frames are admitted in v3, so unknown algorithms are discarded.
error_semantics.UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION: Well-formed settings absent from advertised exact tuples, including contradictory width/auxiliary mode or 450 MHz compression.
error_semantics.INVALID_REQUEST_ID: Request ID is zero or duplicated in the last-16 accepted-request window. A zero ID response echoes zero as the sole correlation exception.
error_semantics.BUSY: CONFIGURE or START during DRAINING or incomplete transport drain.
error_semantics.INTERNAL_ERROR: Device cannot execute an otherwise valid command; any attempted CONFIGURE application is fully rolled back.
error_semantics.CHECKSUM_MISMATCH: Reserved legacy meaning; corrupt checksums are discarded without response.
